content:
Maria Hernandez: FYI saw a weird negative per-invocation cost tile for a customer during model warmup + prefetch. screenshot: https://img.redwood.internal/warmup-ambig.png
Dave Kim: negative cost? ugh. which tenant and timeframe?
Maria Hernandez: tenant `acme-inc`, last ~2 hours. the first ~10 rows in the per-call breakdown show -$0.0029 then it trends back to expected positive. seems like cache credits > allocated amort slice.
Joanne Patel: can you paste the econ row from ingestion? want to see what fields we emit.
Maria Hernandez: sample econ row pulled from staging: ```{
  \"invocation_id\": \"inv-2026-03-23-032\",
  \"tenant_id\": \"acme-inc\",
  \"model_sku\": \"rw-3b-quant\",
  \"tokens_total\": 512,
  \"tokens_cached\": 460,
  \"cache_credits_assigned\": 18,
  \"prefetch_amort_window\": 1200,
  \"timestamp\": 1789799800
}```
Dave Kim: interesting. I suspect the console logic double-applies prefetch credits: ingestion writes `cache_credits_assigned` then the UI also applies a sampled_prefetch_credit when sampling weight >1. if both apply and amort_window small, unit cost can go negative.
Joanne Patel: that matches a bug we saw in a canary last month. ingestion adds credit, UI sampling also adjusted. the immediate fix options: 1) stop UI sampled adjust when `cache_credits_assigned` present, or 2) change ingest to emit canonical signal so UI can be simpler.
Maria Hernandez: I prefer canonical signal from ingest. makes debugging easier and avoids diverging logic.
Dave Kim: what would the ingest signal look like? boolean? enum?
Joanne Patel: propose adding `prefetch_credit_origin` and `prefetch_credit_bucket` strings. origin values: \"ingest\", \"ui\", \"router\". bucket is a small label like \"prefetch-general\". we'll default null for old rows. UI rule: if origin == \"ingest\" skip client-side sampled_prefetch.
Dave Kim: implementation notes: econ pipeline writes to `econ.v1_invocations`. adding two nullable string columns is low risk. Joanna can deploy a migration then write tests. UI: prefer a feature flag `econ_ui_sampling_v2=false` to keep old behavior until migration done.
Maria Hernandez: UX/Support ask: can we add an \"amortization preview\" to the hovercard so support can show how credits are applied across the first N invocations? customers keep screenshots of 'negative cost' and it looks alarming.
Joanne Patel: feasible. UI would visualize the first 50 amortization steps as a small sparkline with notches showing credit slices. API needed: `/econ/preview?tenant=acme-inc&prefetch_id=pf-123` returning compressed list of per-invocation amortized credit amounts.
Dave Kim: performance caution: computing full vectors on-demand for every hover could be expensive. suggest server-side TTL cache keyed on (tenant, prefetch_id) and only compute vector on-demand or on support click. also compress response (e.g., base64 gz) to keep payload small.
Maria Hernandez: agree. default hovercard should remain a single-line summary; add a small \"show amortization\" link to fetch the preview.
ops-bot: deploy started: econometrics-ingest v3.4 -> staging at 1789800200 by @joanne. :rocket:
Joanne Patel: I'll add the two telemetry fields and the feature flag. I will also include migration notes and a simple backfill script to set origin where we can infer it.
Dave Kim: I'll implement the preview endpoint and server TTL cache. will document response schema and include a compact sample.
Maria Hernandez: action list: (1) Joanne: add fields + flag + migration, (2) Dave: preview endpoint + caching + docs, (3) Maria: write short support blurb and hovercard mock. target: patch to staging in 48h and monitor econ dashboards.
Joanne Patel: sounds good. will post PR + staging link.
Dave Kim: +1, will wire up tests and add a small telemetry sanity check to detect negative unit costs over a short window.
Maria Hernandez: thanks all. this should cut down on support noise. cc @product for awareness. :thumbsup:
